clue.text: Retire or dismiss, having almost closed plant

parts.note: to put out a batsman or a rival is to dismiss them
a door that is 'to' is pushed nearly shut, almost closed
grass is a plant

explanation.surface: Someone retires or is fired once the nearly shut factory goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a factory beside 'closed', but it is the green kind; a door 'to' is one pushed almost shut.
explanation.definitionFit: To be put out to grass is to be pensioned off like an old horse, so it is an idiom for retiring.

clue.text: E.g. Pooter is one, but in novel form

definitions.text: E.g. Pooter is one, but in novel form

indicators.note: in novel form says these letters are given a new arrangement

parts.note: e.g. is taken as its letters
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Mr Pooter is a fictional middle-class man, though in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Pooter is the fussy clerk of The Diary of a Nobody. Rearranging EGPOOTERISIBUT gives the answer, and the clue as a whole describes him.
explanation.definitionFit: Pooter is the classic comic portrait of the lower middle class, its small-minded respectability.

clue.text: Ship needs tow at first on slipway

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of tow is used

parts.note: a slipway is a ramp down into water

explanation.surface: A ship has to be towed initially down the slipway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ship' is a tramp steamer, a cargo boat with no fixed route.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is a merchant ship that takes cargo wherever it can.

clue.text: Noble feature of Oxford students

parts.note: an Oxford is a laced shoe, and its upper is part of it
a class is a group of students

explanation.surface: Aristocratic manner is typical of Oxford undergraduates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' suggests the university but is the shoe, whose UPPER is a feature.
explanation.definitionFit: Noble birth puts a person in the upper class, the aristocracy.

clue.text: Hides here to hear girl coming in

indicators.note: coming in means the girl enters the middle of the other word

parts.note: to try a case in court is to hear it
Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone hides here to eavesdrop on a girl entering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hides' looks like a verb but is the noun: animal skins.
explanation.definitionFit: A tannery is where animal skins are cured into leather.

clue.text: Young flier has sweet drink after vigorous activity

indicators.note: after places the drink behind the activity

parts.note: go means energy, vigorous activity
a sling is a sweetened spirit drink, as in gin sling

explanation.surface: A youngster enjoys a sweet cocktail after exertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A gosling is a young goose, a bird that flies.

clue.text: A stream or river

parts.note: a run is a small stream

explanation.surface: A brook or a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Arun is a river in West Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arun flows through Sussex to the Channel.

clue.text: Accountant taken up by Gestapo tortured as convenient victim

indicators.note: taken up by means the accountant is absorbed within the other letters
tortured means twisted, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: CA is chartered accountant

explanation.surface: An accountant is arrested and tortured by the Gestapo as a fall guy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up by' looks like arrest, but it only says the accountant sits inside the rearranged secret police name, which becomes SPEGOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A scapegoat is someone blamed for others' faults, a convenient victim.

clue.text: Don't fear going to London for seed corn

parts.note: to venture is to dare, not to fear
London is the capital of England

explanation.surface: Be brave and head to London to get the grain for planting.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR printed 'com'; the page reads 'corn'. 'Seed corn' is figurative: money invested to start a business.
explanation.definitionFit: Venture capital is money invested in new businesses, the seed from which growth comes.

clue.text: Black music in back-street showing ornamental additions

indicators.note: in places the music inside the reversed street abbreviation
back in back-street tells us to read the street abbreviation from right to left

parts.note: rapping, rap music, grew from black American culture

explanation.surface: Rap music playing in a back alley is dressed up with showy extras.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR printed 'hack-street'; the page reads 'back-street'. 'Black music' sounds like a genre label, and the hyphenated word is split so 'back' acts on 'street', giving TS.
explanation.definitionFit: Trappings are the outward decorations or accessories that go with something.

clue.text: Precious metal seized by American and English customs

indicators.note: something seized by others is held between them, so the metal goes inside

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver, a precious metal

explanation.surface: Silver confiscated by US and British customs officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Customs' suggests border officials but is the definition in the sense of habits.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage means established practice or habit, which is what customs are.

clue.text: Get progressively less light

definitions.meaning: to diminish gradually, narrowing towards an end
a thin candle or wick used to give light

explanation.definitionFit: Taper means both to narrow gradually and a slender candle for lighting.

clue.text: Lamb put back in trailer

indicators.note: put back says the letters found are to be turned round
in shows the letters sit inside the word trailer

explanation.surface: A lamb is loaded back into a horse trailer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lamb' is Charles Lamb, the essayist, who wrote under the pen name Elia; AILE inside 'trailer' turned round gives it.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb signed his Essays of Elia with that pen name.

clue.text: Attend to flap

parts.note: to attend a meeting is to be present, so the first half of that two-word phrase is this verb
the second half of the two-word phrase meaning attend, 'be ___', is this preposition

explanation.surface: Someone is told to deal with a panic.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR printed 'ro'; the page reads 'to'. 'Attend to' tempts as one phrase meaning deal with, but 'to' belongs to the definition, the infinitive 'to flap'.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds beat or flap their wings, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Sheridan's confused speaker, fat and unsuitable

parts.note: Mrs Malaprop in Sheridan's The Rivals garbles words
OS, outsize, is the clothing label for large sizes

explanation.surface: A muddled character from Sheridan, overweight and inappropriate.
explanation.definitionFit: Malapropos means inappropriate or out of place.

clue.text: Cover protecting article, too

indicators.note: protecting means wrapping round, so the article goes inside

parts.note: overly means too, excessively
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A cover shields the item as well.
explanation.definitionFit: An overlay is a covering laid over a surface.

clue.text: Labour soon having hopes like this?

definitions.text: Labour soon having hopes like this?

parts.words: Labour soon having hopes like this?
parts.note: a pregnant woman soon goes into labour, and someone hoping for something awaits it

explanation.definitionFit: Being pregnant and anticipating something are both covered by the one word.

clue.text: Attraction small county has for us

parts.note: Glam is the short form of Glamorgan, a Welsh county
our means belonging to us

explanation.surface: A little county holds charm for people like us.
explanation.walkthrough: Glamorgan is a county in south Wales, cut short to GLAM by 'small'.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamour is alluring charm, a kind of attraction.

clue.text: Lies about attitudes

parts.note: re means about, concerning
poses are bodily attitudes or postures

explanation.surface: Fibs concerning the stances people take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lies' reads as falsehoods but is the verb: lies down, rests.
explanation.definitionFit: To repose is to rest or lie down.

clue.text: Main worry is the mist

parts.note: the main is an old word for the sea
to fret is to worry

explanation.surface: The chief concern is fog.
explanation.walkthrough: A sea fret is a cold sea mist on the North Sea coast of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea fret is a coastal fog rolling in from the sea.

clue.text: Artificial material soft and rubbery? Not at first

parts.note: p, piano, means soft in music

indicators.note: not at first says the opening letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: elastic means stretchy, rubbery

explanation.surface: Is a man-made material soft and rubbery? Not originally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not at first' drops the first letter of the stretchy word, leaving LASTIC; P for soft is the musical marking piano.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic is the standard synthetic, man-made material.

clue.text: Sort of crossing place in chaos

indicators.note: chaos means disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A kind of road crossing is a place of mayhem.
explanation.walkthrough: A pelican crossing is a British pedestrian crossing with traffic lights worked by a button.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelican crossing is a type of signal-controlled pedestrian crossing.

clue.text: King leaves boat to eat out

indicators.note: leaves says the king departs from the word for the boat

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: The king gets off the boat to dine at a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eat out' suggests dining, but it is the definition in the sense of corrode.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to corrode a surface with acid, literally to eat it away.

clue.text: A collection of rabbits, or just part of one

definitions.meaning: in cricket, rabbits are feeble batsmen, and they bunch at the end of the batting order
a rabbit has a short fluffy one at its rear

explanation.definitionFit: The tail is both the weak end of a cricket batting order and the rear part of an animal.

clue.text: Back horse to recover ground

indicators.note: back tells us the word for the horse is read in reverse

parts.note: a pacer is a horse that trots with a pacing gait

explanation.surface: Bet on a horse to win back lost ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reads as betting on the horse, but it is the reversal signal. The definition puns on re-covering ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to summarise, going over the same ground again, read here as re-cover.

clue.text: New driver in vehicle running over a woman

indicators.note: in a down clue, running over means coming above the next part
in places the new driver inside the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
L is the learner plate on a new driver's car

explanation.surface: A learner in a car runs over a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running over' looks like an accident but just puts CLAR above A.
explanation.definitionFit: Clara is a woman's name.

clue.text: For you, it's no longer the point

parts.note: taken as written
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: For your sake, this is no longer the issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' is a compass point, E. 'Thee' is an old word for you, no longer used.
explanation.definitionFit: Thee is the archaic object form of you, no longer in everyday use.

clue.text: Flag taken by hothead of neighbouring country

parts.note: a flag is a type of iris, the plant
the head of hot, its first letter, is H

explanation.surface: A banner is seized by a hothead from the country next door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' suggests a banner but is the yellow flag iris; 'hothead' is read as the head of 'hot'.
explanation.definitionFit: From Britain, Ireland is the neighbouring country, and Irish means belonging to it.

clue.text: Boulder found to be Alpine

parts.note: a boulder is a large rock
to found something is to plant or establish it

explanation.surface: A boulder discovered in the Alps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' reads as discovered, but it means establish, plant.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpine is a small mountain flower grown in rockeries.

clue.text: All classes like royal babies?

parts.note: every social class takes in the high and the low; infant royals are both exalted and tiny

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means people of every rank, and royal babies are both high-born and little.
